packages.title: NAEI UK totals source/end-user QA
facts: NAEI UK-level datasets are produced on both a by-source and end-user basis for greenhouse gases.
International submissions are made on a by-source basis.
NAEI also produces end-user inventories for national and devolved-government greenhouse gas reporting.
By-source assigns emissions to the sector emitting them directly, while end-user reallocates energy-related emissions to users.
Accounting-basis labels must be preserved when comparing NAEI totals.

packages.title: NAEI UK totals reporting-obligation QA
facts: NAEI UK emissions data support international and European reporting obligations.
Greenhouse gas data are reported to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.
NAEI states that its relevant outputs are Accredited Official Statistics.
Local and regional greenhouse gas estimates are also identified as Accredited Official Statistics.
National inventory reporting obligations do not imply parcel-level attribution.

packages.title: NAEI 2026 road transport emission-factor QA
facts: NAEI lists a 2026 publication of fleet-weighted road transport emission factors based on the 2024 NAEI.
The fleet-weighted dataset provides factors by vehicle type.
The dataset covers hot exhaust, cold-start exhaust, evaporative emissions and tyre and brake wear.
NAEI also lists primary NO2 emission factors for road transport in a 2026 version.
Emission factors are conversion inputs and are not direct measurements of parcel emissions.

packages.title: NAEI transport factor versioning QA
facts: The transport emission-factor page was last updated on 20 April 2026.
Factor publications are tied to an inventory base year or version.
Guidance notes accompany the road-transport factor datasets.
Vehicle fleet composition projections are a different product from observed emissions totals.
Using a factor requires compatible activity data and does not justify inferring a land-parcel value.

packages.title: Carbon plan technical-annex modelling QA
facts: The Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan technical annex was updated on 23 June 2026.
The annex contains baseline emissions, emissions analysis, sector modelling and wider analysis.
Policy and sector modelling outputs are analytical estimates rather than direct physical measurements.
Modelled emissions savings must remain distinct from inventory observations.
National policy modelling cannot be used as a parcel emissions measurement without a separate validated binding method.

packages.title: Carbon plan baseline and policy-scope QA
facts: The technical annex provides reference material for the plan's emissions analysis.
Baseline assumptions are part of the modelling framework and should retain their stated scenario context.
Sector modelling can aggregate policies and measures across broad sectors.
Projected or modelled future outcomes must not be labelled as observed emissions.
Any downstream comparison must preserve reference years, sector scope and modelling status.

packages.title: Energy Trends June 2026 timing and scope QA
facts: DESNZ Energy Trends UK total energy was updated on 30 June 2026.
The June 2026 release covers UK energy production, trade and consumption.
Quarterly data are published with a lag and monthly series are also provided.
The page includes tables for indigenous production and inland energy consumption.
Energy quantities are activity data and are not greenhouse-gas emissions unless an explicit emissions methodology is applied.

packages.title: Energy Trends as provisional-emissions input QA
facts: Energy Trends provides current energy statistics used as an input to provisional greenhouse-gas estimates.
Energy production, imports, exports and demand are distinct measures.
Fuel-specific energy statistics must retain their fuel category and period.
Revisions to energy statistics can propagate into later greenhouse-gas estimates.
No parcel emissions value is inferred directly from national energy-balance data.

packages.title: Subnational gas consumption 2024 QA
facts: DESNZ regional and local-authority gas consumption statistics include number of gas meters, total consumption, and mean and median consumption per meter.
The page was updated on 5 May 2026 with a revision notice.
The published series includes gas consumption data through 2024.
Consumption and meter counts are activity indicators, not direct greenhouse-gas measurements.
Local-authority consumption must not be assigned to an individual parcel without a validated allocation method.

packages.title: Subnational gas revision and denominator QA
facts: DESNZ previously revised 2023 non-domestic gas consumption for one North East area.
Revision history demonstrates that subnational energy statistics can change after publication.
Mean and median consumption per meter use a meter-based denominator and must not be presented as totals.
Weather-corrected and non-weather-corrected variants must retain their methodology labels.
Gas consumption cannot be converted to parcel emissions without compatible factors and parcel activity data.

packages.title: Subnational electricity 2024 publication QA
facts: The DESNZ subnational electricity collection includes a 2024 electricity and gas consumption summary report published on 19 December 2025.
The collection provides electricity consumption statistics at subnational geographies.
It includes local-authority and postcode-level products for relevant years.
Electricity consumption is an activity statistic rather than a direct greenhouse-gas measurement.
Grid-emissions attribution requires a separate emissions-factor and accounting-basis decision.

packages.title: Subnational electricity geography and scope QA
facts: Subnational electricity products use defined geographic and meter-data scopes.
Postcode-level estimates and local-authority totals are different aggregation levels.
Publication year and consumption reference year must remain distinct.
Consumption totals must not be presented as territorial emissions.
No property or parcel greenhouse-gas value is inferred from the collection alone.

packages.title: Subnational total final energy aggregation QA
facts: DESNZ sub-national total final energy consumption aggregates electricity, gas, residual fuels and road transport datasets.
The collection provides country, regional and local-authority level energy-consumption statistics.
The latest published local-authority dataset listed on the collection currently covers 2005 to 2023.
The component datasets have different measurement and estimation methods that must retain their provenance.
Aggregated final energy consumption is not itself a greenhouse-gas emissions measurement.

packages.title: Subnational total final energy future-release guard QA
facts: A release for sub-national total final energy consumption during 2024 is announced for 30 July 2026.
Because 30 July 2026 is in the future relative to this batch, 2024 TFEC values must not be treated as observed from that future release.
The currently available collection should remain anchored to the latest actually published dataset.
Future release announcements are scheduling evidence, not statistical observations.
No missing 2024 value is filled by inference.
